term_romaji: ouji no gakusetsu wo tsugumono, ou ga nokoshita kinshi wo tsugumono
en: the one who inherits the king's right, the one who inherits the golden bough the king left behind
why: dialogue_08165 (金枝, 'golden bough') is not in any of the four named glossary files. Web research confirms this is a direct reference to James Frazer's anthropological study 'The Golden Bough' (kinshihen), stated by multiple Japanese sources to be Dewey Novak's favorite book and the thematic source for Eureka Seven's king-succession motif (a king must be slain and his golden bough inherited by the successor). Rendered literally as 'golden bough' (lowercase, in-line reference rather than a proper title) since the line itself is Dewey's own philosophical musing, not a citation of the book's title. Flagging for glossary consolidation as a recurring Dewey/Eureka-Seven thematic term, likely to reappear in later Dewey-centric scenes.
